title: Worked examples: starting early, stepping up, and retirement
objectives: Read the four worked examples and say what each teaches.
Explain why retirement is the most underestimated goal.
body_md:
Worked examples (illustrative). Child's education: ₹20 lakh today, 15 years, 8% inflation → future cost about ₹63.4 lakh; at an assumed 12% (equity-heavy) the monthly SIP needed is about ₹13,300. Same goal, started 5 years late: with 10 years left the SIP is about ₹28,300 — more than double. Same goal, with a 10% yearly step-up: starting SIP about ₹7,700. House down payment: ₹15 lakh today, 5 years, 6% inflation → about ₹20.1 lakh; at an assumed 8% (balanced, debt-heavy) the SIP is about ₹27,300. Retirement: monthly expenses of ₹50,000 today become about ₹2.15 lakh a month in 25 years at 6% inflation. The corpus must fund that, rising every year, for perhaps 25–30 years after retirement. Use a goal calculator with the client's actual numbers; never quote a rule-of-thumb corpus as advice.

| Goal | Cost today | Years | Assumed inflation | Future cost | Assumed return | Monthly SIP needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Child's education | ₹20 lakh | 15 | 8% | ≈ ₹63.4 lakh | 12% (equity-heavy) | ≈ ₹13,300 |
| Same goal, started 5 years late | ₹20 lakh | 10 | 8% | ≈ ₹63.4 lakh* | 12% | ≈ ₹28,300 |
| Same goal, with a 10% yearly step-up | ₹20 lakh | 15 | 8% | ≈ ₹63.4 lakh | 12% | ≈ ₹7,700 to start |
| House down payment | ₹15 lakh | 5 | 6% | ≈ ₹20.1 lakh | 8% (balanced, debt-heavy) | ≈ ₹27,300 |

Three lessons from the numbers: start early — five years' delay more than doubles the SIP for the same goal. Step up — increasing the SIP with income makes a large goal affordable today. Inflation is the real target — planning for today's cost guarantees falling short.
example: Delay costs: education SIP ₹13,300 at 15 years vs ₹28,300 at 10 years — the same target, the same date, more than double the monthly amount.
say: Five years' delay more than doubles the SIP.
Retirement is usually the largest goal; plan it with actual numbers, not rules of thumb.
never: Starting late only raises the SIP a little.
A rule-of-thumb corpus is fine as advice.
